candidates.attacker_control: The archive file's entry metadata is fully attacker-controlled: ZIP Unix symlink entries (mode S_IFLNK) and their link targets are read by commons-compress ZipArchiveEntry.getUnixSymlink() (AbstractZipUnArchiver.resolveSymlink, lines 204-215), and TAR link entries by TarArchiveEntry.getLinkName() (TarUnArchiver.java:112). The subsequent file-entry names are likewise attacker-controlled. Callers such as archive-unpacking Maven plugins extract artifacts obtained from repositories or other externally supplied locations.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for any containment/sanitization of the link target: none exists in AbstractUnArchiver (lines 303-361) or in the zip/tar callers; only the entry name is passed to FileUtils.resolveFile (line 309), which does not validate the target of an already-created symlink. Checked that extraction order permits link-then-write (getEntriesInPhysicalOrder in both execute() variants). Checked that this is not an archive-creation-only concern: ArchiveEntry/DirectoryArchiver symlink handling creates links from a trusted local source, whereas the finding is on the extraction side. Checked version context: pom.xml declares 3.5 and ReleaseNotes.md contains no post-3.4 symlink-hardening entry; there is no symlink-escape guard elsewhere in the Java sources (grep for symlink/createSymbolicLink). File selectors could in principle reject the link entry, but they are optional and unset by default, so they are not a general mitigation.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file write/overwrite on the extracting host under the privileges of the build/application process, escaping the intended extraction directory. Practically this can clobber user or build configuration (e.g. Maven settings, shell profiles, authorized_keys, executables/scripts on PATH) and thereby lead to code execution or credential compromise when a user or CI job unpacks a malicious artifact. Writes are semi-blind (classic Zip Slip limitation), but the write itself is achieved. This matches the known upstream issue fixed after 3.5 in plexus-archiver 4.2.0 (CVE-2019-12402 class).
candidates.prerequisites: The application extracts an untrusted archive with a plexus-archiver UnArchiver (ZipUnArchiver, TarUnArchiver, and subclasses) on a platform where symlink creation succeeds (Unix-like; the archive is processed with Commons Compress on any OS but the link primitive is OS-dependent) into a destination directory. The process must have write permission on the target location; no other configuration is needed. Extraction in physical entry order is used (getEntriesInPhysicalOrder), so the link entry must precede the entry written through it.
candidates.root_cause: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile creates a symlink from the archive entry with an unchecked target (SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(f, new File(symlinkDestination)) at line 327) and then writes subsequent entry contents with new FileOutputStream(f) (line 338) without re-validating containment of the resolved path. Validation, where it exists at all, is applied only to the entry name relative to the destination (FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName), line 309), so a link entry whose target is absolute or otherwise outside dest establishes a redirection that later entries follow through to arbitrary filesystem locations. The ZIP extractor (AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute lines 159-202 / 225-272) and TAR extractor (TarUnArchiver.execute lines 96-118) both pass archive-controlled symlink names from commons-compress (getUnixSymlink / getLinkName) into this sink without checking the link target.
candidates.title: Symlink-based Zip Slip: archive symlink targets are not validated against the extraction directory, allowing writes outside the destination
candidates.trace: ZIP: ZipUnArchiver -> AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute() iterates zf.getEntriesInPhysicalOrder() (line 169); for a Unix-symlink entry resolveSymlink() returns zf.getUnixSymlink(ze) (lines 204-215) and extractFileIfIncluded() (line 217) forwards it to AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile(). Because symlinkDestination is non-empty, SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(f, new File(symlinkDestination)) is executed (line 327), creating a link inside the destination that points anywhere the archive chooses (e.g. an absolute path such as /tmp or $HOME). A later ordinary entry whose name is under that link (e.g. linkname/payload) is resolved by FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) (line 309); parent directories are created (lines 319-323) and content is written via new FileOutputStream(f) (line 338), which the OS resolves through the previously created symlink, so bytes land outside the destination directory. TAR: the identical call is made from TarUnArchiver.execute with te.getName()/te.getLinkName() (lines 112-114).
candidates.unverified: The runtime behavior of FileUtils.resolveFile / SymlinkUtils from the declared external dependencies (plexus-utils 3.0.24, plexus-io 3.0.0) was not inspected or executed, and OS symlink semantics were not exercised; no archive was built or extracted, so the attack chain is inferred from source, not runtime-confirmed. Exploitability on non-Unix platforms is uncertain.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-59 Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following') / CWE-22 Path Traversal (symlink-mediated write outside extraction root)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot (384 files per get_source_scope; 98 Java files per the relation index, index_status complete, 0 missing/omitted files, 0 parse errors). Priority files read in full or in substantial part: AbstractUnArchiver.java, AbstractZipUnArchiver.java, ZipUnArchiver.java, TarUnArchiver.java, DirectoryArchiver.java, ArchiveEntryUtils.java, UnArchiver.java, ArchiveEntry.java excerpts, pom.xml, README.md, ReleaseNotes.md. Used the P1 index only for navigation (find_symbols for extractFile, trace_relations for AbstractUnArchiver callers/overriders) and verified every relevant edge/call in source text; the index reports no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, or runtime reachability, so those were not assumed. The 279 jira/*.json files were only spot-checked (symlink/CVE keyword searches) as historical context, not systematically reviewed, and no such repository instruction or comment was treated as authoritative. Other archiver/unarchiver implementations (bzip2, gzip, snappy, xz, war, ear, jar, diags, manager) were not read line by line and are potential but uninspected areas.
limitations: No code was executed and no archive was crafted/extracted; the finding is a source-evidence lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

External dependency internals (plexus-utils 3.0.24 FileUtils.resolveFile, plexus-io 3.0.0 SymlinkUtils, commons-compress 1.14) are outside the snapshot and were not read; their exact behavior is inferred.
Platform-specific behavior (symlink creation permission, Windows junctions) was not validated.
Zip/tar streaming paths and the remaining compression-format unarchivers, plus ArchiveManager/component wiring (src/main/resources/META-INF/plexus/components.xml), were not fully audited.
Repository-provided jira JSON documents were treated as untrusted context and only keyword-sampled.

rejected_leads.lead: Entry-name path traversal (direct ../ Zip Slip) via FileUtils.resolveFile in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile (line 309)
rejected_leads.reason: The resolveFile call canonicalizes/validates the entry name against the destination root in plexus-utils, and the project explicitly relies on it; without inspecting the external dependency there is no source evidence of a bypass, and it is a weaker lead than the symlink-target gap visible directly in this repository.

rejected_leads.lead: Extractions performed with path prefixes (UnArchiver.extract(String,File); AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute(String,File) lines 226-272) use only name.startsWith(path)
rejected_leads.reason: The prefix comparison selects entries but extraction still flows through the same extractFile sink; its practical effect is subsumed by the reported symlink finding rather than being a distinct issue.

rejected_leads.lead: Archive creation side (DirectoryArchiver.execute lines 90-95; ArchiveEntry.createSymlinkEntry) copies/propagates symlink destinations
rejected_leads.reason: Inputs there come from the local build configuration/filesystem rather than an untrusted archive; no attacker-controlled trust boundary with equivalent evidence was identified.

summary: plexus-archiver 3.5 (pom.xml:13) is an archive creation/extraction library used by Maven plugins. Review of the extraction path shows a single strongest candidate: during extraction of attacker-supplied ZIP/TAR archives, symbolic-link entries are materialized with their archive-provided target without any validation that the link target resolves inside the configured destination directory, and later entries are then written with FileOutputStream through paths that can traverse those symlinks (classic symlink-based Zip Slip). The only containment mechanism present (FileUtils.resolveFile at AbstractUnArchiver.java:309) canonicalizes the entry *name* relative to the destination; it does not constrain the symlink *target* established at AbstractUnArchiver.java:327. Both the ZIP path (AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute -> extractFileIfIncluded -> extractFile, passing ze link name via commons-compress getUnixSymlink) and the TAR path (TarUnArchiver.execute, passing te.getLinkName()) feed unvalidated archive-controlled strings into this sink, so the same root cause affects both formats. No other issue in the snapshot had comparable source evidence; weaker leads are listed as rejected.
